text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's prime minister Zhan Videnov asked his Socialist party for a confidence vote to carry on until January at an all-night meeting of the party's Supreme Council and the Socialist parliamentary group.
Videnov recommended the introduction of a currency board system in Bulgaria proposed by the International Monetary Fund as the only way to halt siphoning of the country's resources. @

-- Greece will ask the European Union's Veterinary Commission to lift the ban on trade and transit of meat and livestock from Bulgaria as an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease in Southeastern Bulgaria has been eliminated, a visiting senior Greek veterinary official said.

-- Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftochim plans a barter deal with Ukrainian companies to secure imports of 120,000 tonnes of wheat for Bulgaria hit by a severe grain shortage against oil products after December 1, a government official said. @

-- Bulgaria's chemical fertiliser maker Himko will export 150,000 tonnes of carbamides to China under a bilateral agreement between Bulgaria and China signed by senior government officials of the two countries in Sofia on Monday.

A Boeing 767-200 passenger plane operated under lease by the Bulgarian state carrier Balkan Airlines has been detained at the Charles de Gaulle airport in Paris because of unpaid bills to the International Air Transport Association topping $6 million and 600,000 French franks maintainence and leasing fees owed to Air France, a Balkan official said.
